message.content:
Here’s a minimal example that does exactly what you asked for – it uses **only** the built‑in `str.split()` method (with its optional *maxsplit* argument): ```python temp = "hello=good=" # your input string # Split once on '=', keeping everything after the first separator in the second element result = temp.split("=", 1) print(result) # → ['hello', 'good='] ``` ### Why this works | Step | Operation | Result | |------|-----------|--------| | 1 | `temp.split("=", 1)` | Splits the string at the **first** `'='`, producing two pieces:
• First piece: all characters before the first `'='` (`"hello")
• Second piece: everything else starting from the character immediately after that `'='` up to the end of the string (`"good="`). | Because we set `maxsplit=1`, any additional `'='` characters (the trailing one in this case) stay inside the second substring rather than creating an extra empty item. This matches the exact output format you requested: ```["hello", "good="]``` --- #### Quick sanity check ```python >>> temp = "foo==bar=baz" >>> temp.split("=", 1) ['foo', '=bar=baz'] >>> temp2 = "a=b=c=d" >>> temp2.split("=", 1) ['a', 'b=c=d'] ``` In each case, the split stops after the very first delimiter, leaving the rest—including any further delimiters—untouched within the second element.
